html:
Chaco Canyon, in northwestern New Mexico, was the centre of the Ancestral Puebloan world from about 850 to about 1150. Its "great houses" were the largest buildings in North America until the 1800s.

In a dry, remote canyon, Chacoans quarried sandstone and hauled tens of thousands of timber beams from mountains up to 80 km away to build about fifteen great houses. The biggest, Pueblo Bonito, had several hundred rooms over four or five storeys, arranged in a D shape around plazas and round ceremonial rooms called kivas. Many rooms seem to have held few people, so the great houses may have been mainly for ceremony, storage and gatherings.

Straight roads ran out from the canyon to "outlier" great houses across the Four Corners region. Some buildings line up with the sun and moon. Chaco traded far: excavators found turquoise, shells from the Pacific, copper bells and scarlet macaws from Mexico, and traces of cacao in drinking jars (see cacao). It was linked, at a distance, to the maize world of Mesoamerica.

A 50-year drought that began around 1130 helped end the system, and people moved away to places like Mesa Verde and later to the Rio Grande. The Hopi and the Pueblo peoples see Chaco as an ancestral home. Their descendants later rose against Spain in the Pueblo Revolt of 1680. Chaco was at its height at the same time as Cahokia in the east.
sum: Chaco Canyon, in northwestern New Mexico, was the centre of the Ancestral Puebloan world from about 850 to about 1150. Its "great houses" were the largest buildings in North America until the 1800s.
